title: Introduce tiered emergency credit and sustained-minimum-throughput enforcer with KV-warmth correlator
author: Maya Singh
description:
Summary: Introduces a multi-tier emergency credit bank and a sustained-minimum-throughput enforcer that together protect committed tenant throughput during multi-pool contention. Adds a lightweight KV-warmth correlator that ties KV-cache hit ratio and warm-pool occupancy to proactive warmlet pre-baking signals. This PR is gated behind the new 'tiered_credit' feature flag and the autoscaler 'min_throughput_enforcer' config.

Motivation and context: We continue to see incidents where short, high-amplitude bursts cause warm-pool churn and evictions that temporarily violate per-tenant throughput SLAs. Existing burst tokens are effective for transient events but do not cover scenarios where pool-level headroom is exhausted and warm-pool replenishment lags due to cold KV caches. This change implements a safety-first flow:
1) Tiered emergency credit: soft -> reserve -> emergency credits that are consumed in order. Emergency credits are a small, decaying buffer reserved for SLA preservation and are paid back on stable utilization periods.
2) Sustained-minimum-throughput enforcer: when a tenant has a defined committed throughput (reservation), the enforcer monitors short-window utilization and proactively reduces non-committed concurrency or routes best-effort requests to lower-cost model variants to preserve the committed floor.
3) KV-warmth correlator: lightweight telemetry aggregation that computes per-pool correlation between KV-cache hit ratio and warmlet warmup success. These correlations are used to adjust warm-pool pre-bake thresholds and prioritize tenants whose request prefixes show high cache sensitivity.

What changed (high level):
- Autoscaler: added TieredCreditBank (soft/reserve/emergency) and reconciler to decouple credit lifecycle from warm-pool allocator.
- Enforcer: new SustainedMinThroughputEnforcer module with admission filters and a pluggable fallback strategy interface (route to quantized model / queue / 429).
- Telemetry: KVWarmthCorrelator job, new telemetry fields (kv_cache_hit_ratio, warmlet_prebake_success_rate, emergency_credit_consumed) and a combined 'elasticity_safety_score' metric emitted for SLO dashboards.
- Tests/bench: unit tests, integration test harness simulating multi-tenant bursts across two pools, and a small perf benchmark measuring p50/p95 under synthetic cold-cache bursts.
- Config/API: new runtime config knobs under dedicated.autoscaler and dedicated.enforcer; admin console controls for tuning emergency credit budgets and canary toggles.

Commits (summary):
- feat(autoscaler): add TieredCreditBank and reconciliation loop
- feat(enforcer): introduce SustainedMinThroughputEnforcer and fallback strategy interface
- feat(telemetry): KVWarmthCorrelator and new telemetry exports
- test(integration): burst-sim harness + synthetic KV miss patterns
- docs: admin guide for configuring the enforcer and credit tiers
- chore: feature-flag gating + migration job for existing token pools

Changed areas / illustrative files:
- services/autoscaler/credit_bank.go
- services/autoscaler/credit_reconciler.go
- services/autoscaler/enforcer/min_throughput_enforcer.go
- services/telemetry/kv_warmth_correlator.go
- operators/helm/dedicated/values.yaml (new knobs)
- integrations/tests/burst_sim/README.md
- integrations/tests/burst_sim/run_bench.sh
- docs/dedicated/emergency-credit.md

Benchmarks & telemetry (before -> after, canary run across 10 medium tenants):
- p50 tail during sustained 120s burst: 28ms -> 26ms (7% improvement)
- p95 tail during same burst: 520ms -> 498ms (4% improvement)
- Incidence of cross-pool eviction leading to SLA drop (measured events per 100 bursts): 12 -> 3 (75% reduction in observed SLA violations in our synthetic harness)
- Emergency credit consumption rate (per-pool): median 0 -> small consumption during peak; credits decay to zero over 15m once headroom restored

Safety, rollout & migration:
- Feature-flagged as 'tiered_credit' + 'min_throughput_enforcer'. Default off for all customers.
- Canary rollout: 5% tenants (internal fleet) for 48h, then 20% for a week, then 100% if metrics stable.
- Backwards compatibility: defaults are conservative (small emergency bucket, enforcer uses queue/429 policy unless tenant opt-in for model fallback). Migration job converts existing burst-token pools to TieredCreditBank with equivalent soft/reserve sizes.
- Observability: new Grafana dashboards and an alert 'Dedicated: EmergencyCreditDepletion' when emergency credits remain >0 for >10m.

Risk and mitigations:
- Risk: overly aggressive enforcer could throttle legitimate traffic. Mitigation: canary gating, per-tenant dry-run mode, and explicit opt-in for model-variant fallback.
- Risk: incorrect correlation heuristics could bias warm-prebake. Mitigation: thresholds are learned with a 24h conservative smoothing window and require delta > 8% before changing pre-bake decisions.

Related work & tickets: Linear ENG-3421 (autoscaler roadmap), ENG-3520 (dedicated SLO incident follow-ups), SUP-789 (customer-reported sustained throughput drops). Also ties to warm-pool prioritizer RFC (internal).

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration harness updated
- [x] Benchmarks included
- [x] Docs updated
- [x] Feature flags added

Notes for reviewers: Focus review on the credit accounting math (credit_bank.go) and the admission path in min_throughput_enforcer.go. The correlator is intentionally low-frequency (30s bucket) to keep overhead minimal. For the fallback strategy, there is a simple default implementation; product has requested a follow-up to plumb tenant-level opt-in for fallback to quantized models.

release_notes: Adds Tiered Emergency Credit system and a Sustained Minimum Throughput Enforcer for Dedicated fleets. Includes KV-warmth telemetry to improve warm-pool pre-bake decisions. Gated behind feature flags; rollout will be gradual. Admin knobs exposed in helm values for dedicated.autoscaler and dedicated.enforcer.
